thought.text: The endpoint is reachable but requires credentials (proper error response). Now let me determine whether `/` and `/energie` are intrinsically broken or if the dev-server cache got polluted by my probes after failed category-page compiles. I'll restart the dev server (permitted: starting the existing installation) for a clean read.

reasoning_content:
The endpoint is reachable (it's returning a proper error response, but I got a 404 instead of 401 — maybe the format of the POST data is different, or the API requires more parameters. Either way, I can't retrieve data without credentials). The README doesn't document the credentials either.

Okay, so I need to determine whether the 500 on `/` and `/energie` is a permanent one, or if it's caused by a transient cache. The install summary recorded them as 200 on first access (fresh compile). My probes after the failed category compile are 500 — this smells like Next.js dev's webpack cache is contaminated with the module-not-found error state.

The cleanest verification: restart `yarn dev` (explicitly permitted as "starting or running an existing install"). Kill the specific PID (1059 yarn dev, 1071 next dev, 1082 next-server — kill the process group), launch a new instance, and test all five pages fresh.

This is within scope: it doesn't install anything or modify files, just runs the existing install. Let's do it carefully.

Actually wait — before restarting, is there a risk that a fresh server will also return 500 on / and /energie? If the webpack cache on disk (.next/cache) is contaminated... The `.next/cache` directory exists. A fresh `next dev` will reuse the on-disk webpack filesystem cache. The "module not found" state for einwohner.csv is legitimate (the file really doesn't exist) and will persist on any recompile of the module graph that includes that component. If /energie's module graph genuinely doesn't include those components, then a fresh compile will be fine.

Let me check what /energie imports — does the energie page import tiles from Mobility/Climate? Let me quickly check app/energie/page.tsx. But the simplest thing is: just restart and test. First kill the old server.
